articles.title: NBA Players with the Most Career Earnings of All Time
articles.summary: During the last couple of decades, the NBA has become an especially large business. Media contracts, sponsorships and other revenue streams have led to teams…
articles.body:
Over the last few decades, the NBA has become an especially large business. Media contracts, sponsorships and other revenue streams have led to teams and players collecting many billions of dollars.

And being a superstar is awfully lucrative. Eleven players have already surpassed $349 million in total NBA earnings, and that number is guaranteed to rise in the coming years.

The list of the NBA's highest-paid players of all time, which unsurprisingly ends with LeBron James, is based on career NBA earnings through the 2025-26 season and is in ascending order.

Russell Westbrook is a prime example of players who have benefited from the NBA's enormous revenue growth.

As his rookie deal on the Oklahoma City Thunder neared its conclusion, Westbrook signed a five-year max extension worth $78.6 million. Five years later, he signed a five-year, $206.8 million deal, which surpassed Curry's as the largest in NBA history.

Though he retired ring-less following the 2025-26 campaign, Westbrook is headed for the Hall of Fame as a nine-time All-NBA selection who was named the league MVP in 2016-17.

The last time we saw Damian Lillard, he'd been helped to the locker room as the Milwaukee Bucks drifted closer to elimination from the 2025 playoffs.

The next time he's on the court, he'll have a new—albeit familiar—uniform.

Lillard rose to stardom with the Portland Trail Blazers, who brought him back on a three-year, $42 million deal in 2025 after the Bucks waived and stretched him. He'd been dealt to Milwaukee in the summer of 2023 after his initial Portland run of 11 seasons, which included a pair of max contracts.

Recovering from an Achilles tear is no simple task, but Lillard is back in a comfortable environment for his return in 2026-27.

Anthony Davis has been involved in two blockbuster trades.

First, the New Orleans Pelicans shipped the All-NBA superstar to the Los Angeles Lakers during the 2019 offseason. Then, on a quiet February 2025 night, news broke out of nowhere that the Lakers were sending Davis to the Dallas Mavericks, with Luka Dončić heading out to Hollywood.

In short, Davis has already navigated a fascinating 14-year career. And it shouldn't be ending anytime soon.

Davis is earning nearly $58.5 million in 2026-27 and has a $62.8 million player option for the 2027-28 campaign. The 33-year-old might have one more substantial contract in his future, too.

Jimmy Butler, the newest addition to the $350 million tier, has been the centerpiece of multiple trades throughout his career.

Butler made his NBA debut with the Chicago Bulls in 2011, developed into a star and signed a $90 million-plus max deal in 2015. The Bulls shipped him to the Minnesota Timberwolves in 2017, but a deteriorating relationship led to another trade—this time to the Philadelphia 76ers—in 2018.

After that lone season in Philly, he landed a four-year, $140.8 million deal with the Miami Heat via a sign-and-trade.

Butler sustained his All-NBA impact over five-plus seasons in Miami and agreed to a three-year, $146.4 million max extension in 2021. Prior to the expiration of that contract, he forced a trade to the Golden State Warriors and immediately declined a player option in favor of a two-year, $111 million extension.

While he enters the 2026-27 campaign rehabbing from a torn ACL, Butler is owed $56.8 million in the second and final year of his Golden State deal.

Once a defense-first stopper for the San Antonio Spurs, Kawhi Leonard quickly developed into an all-around nightmare in the NBA.

"The Claw" earned two Defensive Player of the Year honors and a Finals MVP over seven years in San Antonio. He forced a trade, landed with the Toronto Raptors and carried them to a championship in his lone season there.

Kawhi then signed a max contract to lead the Los Angeles Clippers, his first of three such agreements with the organization.

After an offseason trade sent him back to Toronto in 2026, Leonard is set to earn $50.3 million in 2026-27 with a two-year, $115 million extension to follow.

Chris Paul parlayed being one of the best point guards of his era into several big paydays.

Following his rookie deal, Paul signed a $63.6 million max contract with the New Orleans Hornets in 2008. He got traded to the Los Angeles Clippers three years later and landed a five-year, $107.3 million max extension from them in 2013. He followed that with another four-year, $159.7 million max deal in Houston in 2018 and a four-year, $120 million contract with the Phoenix Suns in 2021.

Those contracts put CP3 on the path toward joining an exclusive club.

After a $30.8 million year in Golden State in 2023-24, he joined the San Antonio Spurs on a $10.5 million deal in 2024-25. That contract lifted Paul past $400 million for his career.

The future Hall of Famer (briefly) returned to the Clips for a final season in 2025-26, appearing in 16 games before retiring.

Unfortunately for Paul George, a seemingly never-ending string of injuries has disrupted a once-incredibly promising NBA career.

Fortunately for him, the direct deposit keeps hitting.

George most recently inked a four-year, $211.6 million pact in free agency with the Philadelphia 76ers in 2024. He'd previously signed max extensions with the Indiana Pacers, Oklahoma City Thunder and Los Angeles Clippers.

Although injuries and a 25-game suspension led him to have two relatively disappointing seasons in Philly, the six-time All-NBA wing has two more $50 million-plus years ahead.

George will top a half-billion dollars in career earnings in 2028 if (when?) he picks up his $56.6 million player option for the 2027-28 campaign.

While splitting the 2025-26 season between the Los Angeles Clippers and Cleveland Cavaliers, James Harden joined the $400 million club and added another layer to his productive career.

Harden began his NBA career on the Oklahoma City Thunder, who dealt him to the Houston Rockets after three seasons. The lefty became an elite scorer in Houston, where he stayed for eight-plus years. Harden has since played for the Brooklyn Nets, Sixers, Clippers and Cavs.

To date, Harden collected his highest single-year salary ($44.3 million) during the 2021-22 campaign, which he split between Brooklyn and Philly. Despite not receiving the huge single-year salaries like others in these rankings, Harden is poised to reach a half-billion in caeer earnings late in the three-year, $96.5 million pact he signed with Cleveland in the 2026 offseason.

The greatest shooter in NBA history, Stephen Curry jumped past the $400 million threshold in the same year as CP3.

Soon enough, Steph could be atop the NBA's all-time earnings list.

Curry has spent all 17 seasons of his career with the Warriors, guiding them to four championships along the way. He's also won a pair of league MVPs, along with a Finals MVP honor in 2022.

Back in 2017, he signed a five-year, $201.2 million contract, which was the largest deal in NBA history at the time. After the 2022 season, Curry inked a four-year, $215.4 million pact.

Curry is far from finished cashing checks, too. He's due $62.6 million in 2026-27 , and he just signed a two-year extension worth $116 million.

Kevin Durant may reach $600 million in career earnings first, but Curry is the first NBA player ever to ink a contract that would propel him beyond that incredible mark.

You see that number. The wildest part is that Kevin Durant has actually left money on the table.

When he left Oklahoma City for Golden State, he didn't sign max contracts. Durant kept accepting below-market deals to keep the Warriors' core together, which helped lead to two NBA titles. He exited both of the Dubs' championship runs as the Finals MVP, too.

Durant finally inked a max offer in 2019, joining the Brooklyn Nets on a four-year, $164.3 million pact in a sign-and-trade.

His next extension—which he signed in Brooklyn before he joined the Phoenix Suns and was later traded to the Rockets—was worth $194.2 million over four seasons. He then re-upped with Houston on a two-year, $90 million agreement that runs through 2027-28, pending a player option.

To absolutely nobody's shock, LeBron James headlines this list.

Not only is he LeBron freaking James , he's the longest-tenured player of this revenue-exploding era. The King entered the NBA in 2003, so he's signed 10 contracts across 23 combined seasons on the Cavaliers, Heat, Cavs again, Lakers and now 76ers.

LeBron, as Durant did in Golden State several years later, took a discount with Miami to allow a stronger roster. That strategy paid on-court dividends with two NBA titles, as well.

Over the last decade, James has prioritized short-term contracts that have maximized both his salary and flexibility (read: leverage).

While collecting $48.7 million in 2024-25, he made history as the first player to surpass a half-billion dollars in NBA earnings.

LeBron left L.A. for the Sixers in the summer of 2026, taking just $7.9 million over two seasons to play alongside Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey.

articles.title: Anthony Edwards, LaMelo Ball and the Timberwolves' plan to unleash their most polarizing pairing yet
articles.summary: In Minnesota, creating one of the league's most dynamic duos in recent times was born out of necessity. Will it work?
articles.body:
MINNEAPOLIS — Midway through a conversation about the Minnesota Timberwolves' busy summer and their attempt to stage a Western Conference coup behind Anthony Edwards and LaMelo Ball, Chris Finch is forced to pivot.

The 56-year-old head coach, seated comfortably in his office donning a plain black hoodie and gray shorts, adjusts his posture. His standard humdrum demeanor, suitable for the Minnesota skies in early October, has now been replaced by unbridled joy.

The former point guard, NBA champion and assistant coach spent just one season with Finch in New Orleans nearly a decade ago. But the unmistakable comparisons to his newest floor general, Ball — from their cerebral approach to the game to their fiery on-court personality and the eccentric in between — bring him to a familiar place.

"They're such high IQ [players]," he says, his memory harkening back. "You don't want to get in their way; you want to give them freedom. The more freedom you give players, the more they gravitate to the things they already do well, and then when they don't, it's easy to see and coach them back to where you need them to be. Rondo was a great example, very much like a quarterback making all the reads, [but] it's a collaborative thing. I'm excited because I see a lot of that with LaMelo."

The more Finch envisions the specifics of just how the Edwards-Ball tandem can work, a Midwestern blend of old-school principles and modern half-court ideologies, the more it's clear that his desire to revamp Minny's backcourt — creating one of the league's most dynamic duos in recent times — was born out of necessity. Less than six months ago, the Wolves' latest postseason heartbreak, a second-round slip to the Spurs, had created an inflection point. From a micro lens, their menacing frontcourt had been neutralized by Victor Wembanyama's mere presence, rendering Julius Randle inefficient and Rudy Gobert ineffective. A Finals-worthy opponent had bested them in a battle of wits and fortitude.

But on a macro level, the elephant in the room — that this team, as currently constructed, simply wasn't good enough to seriously contend — had become unavoidable. Their best chances of playing in June had been shot down in consecutive seasons, clear signs of a group not ready to go the distance. The roster, which had loaded up on physicality and brute force, had waned in the backcourt; Minnesota's ball-handlers were either too old (Mike Conley), too inexperienced (Rob Dillingham) or too inconsistent (Bones Hyland) to warrant night-to-night threats. The other option, Donte DiVincenzo, was a few weeks removed from a torn right Achilles. Edwards' workload had reached insurmountable levels over time, resulting in the 25-year-old missing time during both the regular season and playoffs.

Finch doesn't necessarily view the past six seasons as an organizational window — he believes each season has its own "distinct personality." But the synergy that has existed between himself, general manager Matt Lloyd and president of basketball operations Tim Connelly meant there was alignment for a change, and not one simply to ameliorate Edwards and ward off rumors of a desire for a move elsewhere.

Ball checked off multiple boxes: a leader of a top-five offense in the NBA with a high assist rate and low turnover rate, a natural creator who could afford Edwards more time off the ball, a bigger frame to keep the team's positional size objectives afloat, the potential of unlocking Gobert and Jaden McDaniels more, and the ability to play faster, ultimately allowing Edwards to settle into his off-guard role.

"I'm a natural 2-guard at heart," Edwards said on media day. "I never thought I could develop any point guard skills. I know Finchy harps on me for passing the ball, but now we got LaMelo so I'm happy."

"We felt that they could both play with a joy that would be reflective of one another," Finch adds. "Anthony loves to root for his teammates; he's a fun-spirited but competitive guy, and we felt (LaMelo) might help lighten the mood around Anthony a little bit. We also felt like Anthony's competitive seriousness could also help LaMelo.

"They both still have things that they need to do to take the next step as incredible as they are, but you know they're always gonna do it with a smile on their face, and we felt that was gonna be contagious."

Because the process of assimilating a star guard into another team's culture takes time — especially given the age-old adage of point guards being extensions of the coach on the floor — Finch has leaned heavily on Edwards throughout the process. The two have become extremely close since Finch first took the job in 2021. The highs. The lows. The wins. The losses. They have been there for each other every step of the way. But following the Wolves' most recent postseason exit, the nature of their conversations varied over the summer.

First, Finch wanted Edwards to get healthy, praising his valiant efforts to return to the floor after nagging hamstring and knee issues, but urged him to continue to take care of his body. Second, as the complexion of the roster and outlook changed, the two spoke often about the sheer potential that was building and the excitement of a new challenge. But most importantly, Finch hammered home the point that, despite a world of ongoing change around Edwards, the superstar didn't need to modify or alter who he was.

There was a natural impulse for Edwards to try and become something he's not in an attempt to drag a franchise to unforeseen heights, perhaps forcing himself to speak up more and become a booming locker room voice. But in Finch's view there was enough of a veteran presence on the team, enough collective experience, that simply excelling in the smaller areas and leading by example would be enough. And in turn, that would aid Ball's orientation. The two stars had always been fond of one another coming up in the high school and AAU circuit before being drafted first and third overall in 2020, but this was different.

"Anthony wants this to be a huge success, so allowing LaMelo to come in and be LaMelo is the first and most important thing," Finch says. "It's not asking him to change his game at all, in any way, shape or form. He's willing to make sacrifices knowing that the ball will be out of his hands more, but ultimately, he and others will all benefit from it. And stoking the competitiveness in each other, they've been good at that. Whether it's been post-practice or post-workout shooting, going at each other in open runs in the summertime and also spending time off the floor."

Such a journey, however, isn't left up to the new star duo alone. Before every season, Finch jots down a list of personal coaching goals he wants to achieve. And these aren't benchmarks like, say, finishing as a top-10 team in 3-point shooting or leading the league in turnovers. Finch has specific "behavioral goals" he wants to hit, like becoming closer with his young players, handling losses and adversity better, working on relations with league officiating or being more receptive to schematic tweaks and outside input. During the year, Finch will have regular check-ins with Minnesota's mental performance team to track his progress.

"You learn stuff about yourself all the time, particularly in a job that's extremely humbling," he says. "I write them down, keep them close to me."

A dedication to improving himself makes mapping out the Wolves' new attack plan easier. Minnesota finished last season ranked 11th in pace and 14th in offensive efficiency, half-court points per possession and transition frequency. With Ball under center, Finch wants his group to play faster, much faster. As the game has evolved, both the analytics and eye test show that some of the best shots come earlier in the shot clock before opposing defenses can be set up. Losing talents like Randle and Naz Reid stings, but the ability to offset that with speed is quite appealing to Minnesota's coaching staff. Edwards and Ball are elite at getting to the rim, reserve guard Ayo Dosunmu can probe defenses and create paint touches and their new-look frontcourt — Jonathan Kuminga, McDaniels and Gobert — all can create from the trail, a huge area of focus for Finch. Parts of the playbook have also been simplified given Ball's whirlwind experience playing for three head coaches in Charlotte.

"I listen, you know what I'm saying," Ball said earlier this week about learning a new system. "Just try to get the most info, learn day by day, get 1% better. Take what you learn from that day, bring it to the next day, and so on."

The Wolves' opening preseason game, a comfortable 116-97 win over the Bucks , offered additional insight into Finch's plans to utilize his prolific pairing. After crossing half-court, Edwards screened for Ball on several occasions, either flaring out to the wing or rolling to the rim after making contact. Guard-to-guard actions are effective given their quickness and timing, but their size gives them an increased advantage.

Finch says both will share the floor quite often, but there are still some clear elements of staggering in play — similar to how Mike D'Antoni ran Houston's offense under Chris Paul and James Harden. Against Milwaukee, both Edwards and Ball started and remained on the floor until about the five-minute mark, when Ball was subbed out. He then checked back in about 90 seconds later for Edwards and stayed with the second unit until the 10-minute mark in the second quarter, when he subbed out for Edwards again. Both would play the final four minutes together. The duo combined for 25 points, 8 rebounds and 5 assists in just under 20 minutes of action.

"He was great tonight," Edwards said to reporters on Ball's unofficial debut. "Y'all know. He plays like his hair is on fire. He gets everybody involved. He talked more than I expected throughout the game. That's another big one for me, especially because I love people who talk. Let us know what you see."

In October, there's no greater time for a team-in-waiting. The vibes are high. The chemistry is through the roof. So then, are the expectations. Increased parity in recent years has led several teams to believe that anything is possible once the playoffs start, but the price of contention remains high. Edwards and Ball, for all their talent and experience, are still young players who will continue to learn more about themselves and, in turn, each other. There will be bumps and bruises along the way — but there's no internal limit on what they can achieve together.

"There's tremendous potential for those guys to be dynamic, explosive, entertaining, all of that stuff," Finch says. "We're looking at idealized versions of everybody when we make these kinds of guesses, but that's also part of our job to try and predict these things. I think the ceiling is extremely high, but we have lots of work to do to solidify it."

articles.title: 76ers' Ariel Hukporti Suffers Season-Ending Injury, Updated Depth Chart and Salary Cap Space
articles.summary: The Philadelphia 76ers announced that center Ariel Hukporti suffered a season-ending torn right Achilles tendon during his team's preseason opener on Monday evening against the New York Knicks.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia 76ers announced that center Ariel Hukporti suffered a season-ending torn right Achilles tendon during his team's preseason opener on Monday evening against the New York Knicks.

Hukporti, who played his first two seasons with the New York Knicks, signed a one-year, $3.4 million deal with the 76ers in July. The 24-year-old played 54 games last year (five starts) for the NBA champions.

Here's a look at the 76ers' current depth chart with Hukporti out for the year.

SF: Jaylen Brown, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, Justin Edwards

PF: LeBron James, Dean Wade, Dominick Barlow

C: Joel Embiid, Adem Bona, Jabari Walker

The 76ers are over the cap by $53.9 million, per Spotrac . They have $1.8 million in space below the first apron and $14.5 million below the second apron.

ESPN's Bobby Marks provided more insight on the 76ers' cap outlook following the news on Hukporti.

The 76ers are currently thin at center with backup Adem Bona out due to a sprain in his left foot suffered while playing for Turkey during World Cup qualifiers this summer, per Tony Jones of The Athletic.

Bona did not play Monday. ESPN's Dave McMenamin reported on Oct. 1 that Bona would be reevaluated in the next few days.

Jones gave insight Monday into what the 76ers might do at center without Hukporti, noting Jabari Walker and Dominick Barlow could be bigger factors behind Embiid.

The 6'7", 237-pound Walker played 64 games (six starts) for the 76ers last year, averaging 4.3 points and 3.0 rebounds per game in 11.9 minutes per game.

The 6'9", 215-pound Barlow played 71 games and made 59 starts for last year's 76ers team. He averaged 7.7 points and 4.8 rebounds per game.

The 76ers begin their season on Tuesday, Oct. 20 at the Knicks.

articles.title: 76ers' Ariel Hukporti out for season after rupturing right Achilles tendon in preseason opener
articles.summary: The Sixers' reserve center had to be helped off the floor, and left the arena on crutches and in a walking boot.
articles.body:
Philadelphia 76ers center Ariel Hukporti will miss the entire 2026-27 NBA season after rupturing his right Achilles tendon less than five minutes into the team's first NBA preseason game against the New York Knicks on Monday, the team announced Tuesday .

Hukporti, who left the Knicks to sign a one-year, $3.4 million deal with the 76ers in free agency this summer, got the start in Philadelphia on Monday in place of Joel Embiid, who joined LeBron James and Tyrese Maxey among several other Sixers who didn't suit up for the preseason opener. With the score tied at 10 and just over seven minutes remaining in the first quarter, Hukporti stepped out to guard former teammate Karl-Anthony Towns at the 3-point arc. As Jalen Brunson curled around a Towns screen, Hukporti dropped back toward the paint to cut off the passing lane.

When Towns held onto the ball and rose up to shoot it, Hukporti planted on his right foot and tried to sprint out to contest the shot. He immediately stopped in his tracks, though, turning to look behind him as he reached for his right ankle and fell to the floor.

After the Knicks scored on the possession, Hukporti remained seated, holding onto his right heel. The Sixers called a timeout, as players and coaches from both teams circled around the fallen big man. Hukporti would need help to get to his feet; seemingly unable to put any weight on his right leg, he leaned on Towns and a member of the coaching staff to help him hop off the floor and back to the locker room. He was ruled out for the remainder of the game, which the Sixers won, 120-97 .

"I just saw him for a little bit during the game and gave him a big hug," Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said after Monday's game, according to Noah Levick of NBC Sports Philadelphia . "He's been a joy to coach in the short time he's been here. Really a good dude. We'll just hope for the best."

Hukporti left the arena on crutches and in a walking boot , leaving both his former and current teammates fearing the worst. Follow-up imaging on Tuesday confirmed those fears, ending the young center's season before it ever really got started.

"Definitely heartbreaking," Brunson said, according to Stefan Bondy of the New York Post . "When I came back in the locker room, I went to go check on him. Sad to see. Obviously, we'll pray for him."

"Damn, that messed me up, honestly," a "visibly distraught" Jabari Walker said, according to Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice . "Yeah, that messed me up. That's tough [...] I met him early on, and he was just one of the guys right away that was just super cool, outgoing. If you know him, you know he's going to talk to you. He's lively, same version every day. So it's a deeper connection when you already know somebody on that level. It's more investment. So when I heard that news, it's tough. Much love to Ariel."

A second-round pick out of Germany in the 2024 NBA Draft, the 7-foot Hukporti averaged 2.1 points and 2.7 rebounds in 9.1 minutes per game across two seasons in New York. The 24-year-old served as a third-string center on the team that won the 2026 NBA championship behind Towns and Mitchell Robinson before joining Philadelphia to pair with Adem Bona in backing up Embiid — an opportunity for an increased role that has now been dashed.

Losing Hukporti, who will undergo surgery on Tuesday, deals a significant blow to a Sixers team that is already without third-year center Bona, who has missed the start of training camp after suffering a left foot sprain playing for the Turkish national team this summer.

Philadelphia signed Hukporti specifically to help bolster its backup center spot behind the oft-injured Embiid, who has missed 150 games over the last three seasons. Replacing him could prove tricky for the Sixers, who sit just $1.83 million below the first apron , at which they're hard-capped after using their nontaxpayer midlevel exception to sign Cavaliers forward Dean Wade in free agency.

That's not enough space to sign a player to a veteran's minimum-salaried contract at this point; come December, according to Derek Bodner of PHLY Sports , they'll be able to sign someone to a pro-rated deal for the rest of the season. Until then, though, unless they make another roster move, Nurse and Co. will have to find other options to fill the void, including playing smaller with Walker, Dominick Barlow and perhaps LeBron at the 5 — all while crossing their fingers and hoping that the notably slimmed down Embiid can stay healthy and fully ambulatory until new Sixers general manager Mike Gansey can find a way to bring in some reinforcements.

articles.title: LeBron James Reacts to Rumor He Called Out Joel Embiid for Being 'Minutes' Late to 76ers Practice
articles.summary: LeBron James has officially responded to rumors that he called out Joel Embiid for being late to 76ers practice.
articles.body:
LeBron James has officially responded to rumors that he called out Joel Embiid for being late to 76ers practice.

In an Instagram post on Tuesday, James wrote, "🧢! He ain't been late so stop the lies."

LeBron James Gets Trolled by Michael Che

NBA broadcaster Mike Breen reported during Monday's preseason game between the 76ers and New York Knicks that James let Embiid "hear it" during a recent 76ers practice after Embiid was late to the session.

Breen revealed during the game broadcast that "somebody" told him about the encounter before the game.

"They were out ready to practice, Joel Embiid walked out on the court a couple of minutes late and LeBron let him hear it," Breen reported.

James and Embiid are entering their first year as teammates following a busy offseason in which the 76ers added Jaylen Brown and the NBA's all-time leading scorer to a core that includes Tyrese Maxey, VJ Edgecombe and Embiid.

While Embiid remains a dominant offensive force for Philadelphia when healthy, his punctuality has been an issue in the past.

In Nov. 2024, Maxey reportedly criticized Embiid for being late "for everything" and "challenged" him to be on time for team activities moving forward.

As for James, he's known for his meticulous workout regimen in order to prepare for each season. That hasn't changed entering his 24th year in the NBA, as Edgecombe reflected on the first time he saw James in the locker room before practice.

"He was in there before everybody," Edgecombe said, per ESPN's Dave McMenamin . "As usual."

With expectations high for the 76ers entering their 2026-27 campaign, James has prioritized accountability among his new teammates.

"The only thing that matters is what we preach every day and how we're gonna hold each other accountable," James said during a Sept. 25 episode of his Mind the Game podcast.

The 76ers have three more preseason games ahead of them before they open the regular season against the Knicks on Oct. 20.

articles.title: 5-Star Center Darius Wabbington Announces CBB Commitment Between UNC, Indiana, Illinois, More
articles.summary: Darius Wabbington, a 5-star center out of the class of 2027, has announced his college basketball commitment.
articles.body:
Darius Wabbington, a 5-star center out of the class of 2027, has announced his college basketball commitment.

Per ESPN's Jeff Borzello, Wabbington committed to Indiana over North Carolina, Illinois, Kentucky and more.

According to 247Sports' composite rankings , Wabbington is the No. 13 player in the country and the No. 2 center in the class of 2027. He is the Hoosiers' third-highest recruit in program history, according to 247Sports .

"I'm going to Indiana University and I chose there because the plan they have for me and the trust that the entire organization has in me," Wabbington told Dushawn London of 247Sports.

Wabbington had an official visit to Indiana last month before taking trips to Illinois and Arizona. Ultimately, he decided Bloomington was the place for him.

Wabbington marks Indiana's third commit out of the class of 2027, joining 4-star point guard Chase Branham and Felix Keihlneker out of Germany.

The Hoosiers had success in recruiting last year, putting together the No. 8-ranked recruiting class, according to 247Sports . Indiana also brought in a number of highly coveted players through the transfer portal, with former Alabama forward Aiden Sherrell highlighting the group.

The Hoosiers are looking to return to being the powerhouse they once were, and landing recruits like Wabbington is a good start, but Indiana still has plenty of work to do.

In his first season as head coach, Darian DeVries finished 18-14 overall and 9-11 in conference play. Indiana missed the NCAA tournament for the third consecutive season.

The second year of the Devries era tips off on Nov. 2 with a matchup against Eastern Illinois.

articles.title: La Laguna Tenerife no da la talla ante el London Lions (89-77)

articles.summary: Shermadini (18+3) y Tijani (16+3) no bastan en un día discreto de Huertas (2+1+6)
articles.body: El London Lions frenó al La Laguna Tenerife en su estreno europeo a domicilio. Los británicos impusieron su ley en el Copper Box Arena después de un segundo cuarto demoledor (28-23) que volteó el marcador y puso al conjunto local al mando. Tenerife sólo pudo llevarse el primer parcial (18-19) y acabó cediendo ante el empuje de unos Lions que fueron de menos a más. El gran verdugo tuvo nombre y apellidos: Thomas Kennedy. El pívot fue una pesadilla cerca del aro y firmó 26 puntos con un espectacular 12/13 en tiros de dos, además de capturar ocho rebotes para alcanzar los 34 de valoración. A su lado, Keenan Evans añadió 21 puntos y Devante Jones, otros 15. Una batería ofensiva que castigó una y otra vez a un Tenerife incapaz de contener el juego interior británico. El equipo de Jaka Lakovic encontró en Giorgi Shermadini a su principal argumento ofensivo. El georgiano terminó con 18 puntos sin fallo en los tiros de dos (7/7), mientras que TJ Bamba aportó 16 y Tim Abromaitis y Vince Hunter sumaron 10 cada uno. Pero faltó acierto exterior: Kyle Guy se quedó en nueve puntos con un 1/9 desde el triple y Marcelinho Huertas, pese a repartir seis asistencias, apenas anotó dos puntos. El tiro libre terminó de inclinar la balanza. Tenerife dispuso de 21 lanzamientos y sólo convirtió 11, mientras que London fue mucho más contundente desde la línea: 28/36, 17 tiros libres anotados más que su rival. Una diferencia demasiado grande para un partido que terminó decidiéndose por detalles y por la mayor agresividad de los locales atacando el aro. El 89-77 deja al Tenerife con la primera derrota europea de la temporada y evidencia el peaje de jugar lejos de casa. Los Lions sobrevivieron a su desacierto desde el perímetro (7/25 en triples), pero encontraron el camino por dentro y no perdonaron desde la línea. Kennedy puso el músculo, Evans la pólvora y Londres acabó imponiendo su ley. articles.title: Without LeBron James, Bronny has chance to prove he really belongs
articles.summary: You could tell Bronny James needed this. LeBron James fulfilled his dream of becoming the first NBA player to play alongside his son. Now it’s Bronny’s turn...
articles.body:
You could tell Bronny James needed this.

LeBron James fulfilled his dream of becoming the first NBA player to play alongside his son.

Now it's Bronny's turn to fulfill his dream.

He wants to be respected as an NBA player. And we all know that was a nearly impossible task while sharing a locker room with LeBron, who's not only his dad but also one of the greatest basketball players of all time.

Bronny turned 22 years old on Tuesday. He's entering his third season with the Lakers. He's the third- longest-tenured player on the roster. And he's no longer under his father's shadow after LeBron left for the 76ers in free agency over the summer.

In the Lakers' first preseason game on Monday against the Kings , Bronny had three points, five rebounds, two assists, one blocked shot and one turnover in 16 minutes.

It wasn't a flashy statline by any means, especially not during a time of the year when coaches are experimenting with different lineups, stars are shaking off rust and fringe players are trying to earn a roster spot.

But Bronny doesn't need to be flashy. He needs to do the small things. He needs to be dependable. Consistent. He needs to undisputedly prove that he's an NBA player without being in his father's oversized orbit.

He has been trying to blaze that path for a while. He has been trying to shake off the nepotism label. He has been keeping his head down and putting in the work.

After he had a 17-point, five-rebound and three-assist performance against the Bucks as a rookie in March 2025, ESPN analyst Stephen A. Smith even acknowledged that he "might have been wrong" about Bronny's NBA readiness.

Last season, Bronny went on to earn playoff minutes against the Rockets and Thunder.

This season, he has a new challenge. Really, a new opportunity.

He finally can prove that his NBA career no longer has anything to do with his father. LeBron is out of the locker room. Bronny is on his own.

"I mean, he's got his own path, and I got my own," Bronny said at Lakers media day when asked about LeBron leaving the Lakers. "So he knows that I want to make a name for myself and continue my career and keep growing as a player. And he knows that I want to focus on that."

Bronny spent the first week of Lakers training camp trying to build his "defensive instinct."

During the offseason, he devoted himself to working on his craft, with one of the focuses being his jump shot.

"I've been in the gym all summer working on fluidity and the speed of my release, stuff like that, moving," Bronny said at Lakers practice on Saturday. "Tied into that, just running a lot. I'm the same weight, 215 or 220-ish, but still slim so I can move fast. Just getting in the gym every day and continuing to keep a routine."

Bronny can finally show the world what he can do without accusations that his father is holding the door open for him. The cries of nepotism will be quieted if he can thrive while LeBron is on the other side of the country.

Really, ever since Bronny entered the league as the the 55th overall pick by the Lakers in the 2024 NBA Draft, he has had an impossible task.

LeBron has been the face of the league for two decades. He gets treated differently by players and staffers. Imagine being his son. Imagine being a rookie or a second-year player sharing a locker room with him .

While Bronny spent the last few years talking about how cool it was to play with his father, it's obvious that he's also excited to now have a chance to step out from under his father's enormous shadow.

"I think for me, just the motivating factor of creating my own path and my own career makes me want to get up every day and work hard," Bronny said.

He went from having a cardiac arrest that threatened his life as an incoming freshman at USC to making good plays in NBA games. He's the son of a billionaire. He doesn't need the scrutiny and pressure of being LeBron James' son in the NBA. He's doing this because he loves this.

He earned the respect of his coaches and teammates. He's likable. He's humble.

But his detractors were always the loudest ones in the echo chamber.

Even though Bronny was playing better than nearly anyone picked near him in the draft, he was always held to a different standard. He was LeBron's kid. His bloodline meant that he had to suffer a spotlight that wasn't meant for him.

Well, that spotlight has moved to Philadelphia.

Bronny is now on his own to forge relationships and earn playing time without one of the most powerful people on the planet standing in the room watching.

And if he does that, his detractors will finally be screaming into a void.

And Bronny now has his first real chance to prove he's where he's supposed to be.

articles.title: Man files lawsuit against USC, coach Eric Musselman after beach altercation during Trojans photoshoot
articles.summary: Eric Musselman confronted a man using a metal detector on the beach during a team photoshoot last month.
articles.body:
The man who was involved in a heated beach dispute with USC men's basketball coach Eric Musselman last month has filed a lawsuit against both the coach and the school.

Gary Gosnell, who runs a popular YouTube channel, "Gary's Metal Detecting," filed a lawsuit in Los Angeles on Monday, according to the California Post . Gosnell said Musselman verbally berated him in Manhattan Beach on Sept. 13, and that he suffered "severe emotional and psychological distress" and "a significant deterioration of his health."

"I know the responsibilities that come with my role, and while I was trying to step in and support my coach, I definitely should have handled this situation better and will learn from this for the future," Musselman said of the incident in a statement last week.

Gosnell was walking along the shore in Manhattan Beach on the morning of Sept. 13 while using a metal detector. He ended up walking near a photo shoot for the Trojans' basketball team. That's when Gosnell said that assistant coach Will Conroy approached him and tried to get him to move.

"Mr. Gosnell explained that he was simply passing through and would move on once he finished what he was doing, noting that it was a public beach and that he could be wherever he wanted to be," the lawsuit said.

After Conroy threatened him, Gosnell said that Musselman jumped in and started "screaming profanities" in his face.

"Musselman shouted at Mr. Gosnell to '[s]hut the f*** up,' called him a 'f***ing d***head,' and threatened that '[s]omebody should f***ing drop your ass is what should happen,'" the lawsuit said.

The incident ended soon after. Gosnell filmed the encounter, too.

Gosnell, 57, said that he has undergone three spine surgeries, a knee surgery and multiple foot surgeries. He has suffered from post-traumatic stress disorder, and "holds a disabled person parking placard."

He is suing both Musselman and Conroy, claiming that the two caused him "severe emotional and psychological distress, including fear, anxiety and humiliation." He also said that it led to a resurgence and aggravation of his PTSD symptoms." Gosnell is also suing USC, claiming that the school should have supervised Musselman better.

"USC knew or should have known that Musselman had a propensity to engage in unprovoked, profane, hostile, and intimidating verbal outbursts directed at others," Gosnell's lawsuit stated, "and that this propensity created a particular risk that Musselman would verbally abuse, threaten, and intimidate persons with whom he interacted in the course of his duties, including members of the public encountered during team activities."

The incident came just before a separate lawsuit was filed against Musselman and USC regarding former star Chad Baker-Mazara, who left USC during the final stretch of the regular season last spring. He claimed that Musselman went off on a "profanity-laced, racially charged" tirade against him in the locker room.

Musselman was hired to take over at USC before the 2024-25 campaign after spending five years at Arkansas. The Trojans went 18-14 last season, and have yet to make the NCAA tournament under his watch.

USC will open the season against Milwaukee on Nov. 2.

articles.title: Bronny James Gets Unexpected Lakers Trade News After Preseason Game
articles.summary: Bronny James' performance in the Lakers' preseason game could change the outlook on a potential trade or roster cut before the season begins. The post Bronny...
articles.body:
Third-year guard Bronny James didn't show out in his first preseason game of the year for the Los Angeles Lakers, but the 21-year-old might have done enough to save himself from a trade or roster cut before the regular season begins.

Though James' position as the Lakers' final roster cut isn't at the same level compared to guys like Jaden Hardy or Dalton Knecht, there's still an outside chance the team waves him before the season begins.

Additionally, recent reports indicate the Lakers could trade the son of LeBron James before the season starts, but the young guard may have saved himself from that fate after what was seen in the team's preseason opener against the Sacramento Kings.

Bronny James Gets Unexpected Trade, Roster Cut News After Preseason Game

Again, though James isn't on the same tier as Knecht or Hardy in terms of the pressure of being the Lakers' final roster cut, he can't be ruled out as the last player the team waives to get to the 15-man roster limit set by the league.

However, after the Lakers' first preseason game against the Kings, James could be saving himself from a trade or roster cut before the regular season starts.

When writing about his takeaways from Los Angeles' Monday night win over Sacramento in what was the first time a majority of this new-look roster was seen on the court in a competitive setting, Svyatoslav Rovenchuck believes 'Bronny James is closer to the Lakers rotation than getting cut or traded.'

"One of the biggest storylines that has been following the Lakers throughout the offseason involves questioning how they intend to finalize the roster . For anyone thinking it would come in the form of getting rid of Bronny James, that appears to be a tough sell after Monday night."

James only shot 1/5 from the field, scoring three points, grabbing five rebounds, and dishing out two assists in 16 minutes. However, by getting put into the game before guys like Knecht and Hardy, Rovenchuk thinks James ranks ahead of those two for saving himself from the final roster cut, and could be even closer to finding himself playing more minutes in the Lakers' upcoming campaign.

"James saw the court before Jaden Hardy or Dalton Knecht. Those are both guys many have assumed are competing with him to stay on the roster," he added. "If the matchup against the Kings was an indicator, Bronny is leading that group. Hardy did not see minutes until the third quarter. Knecht only touched the floor in the fourth. James looks to be fairly safe by comparison to those Lakers peers."

Scott Polacek of Bleacher Report also felt James did enough to at least get closer to solidifying himself on the Lakers roster rather than becoming a trade or cut candidate.

"While the USC product certainly didn't take over as a scorer, he impacted the game in other ways by crashing the boards and dishing out multiple assists," he wrote. "He also hit from three-point range. That three-point shooting will be important if he is going to earn playing time this season, as the defensive attention Dončić draws should create a number of open looks."

One preseason game does not guarantee anything, however. James could still very well be the one name the Lakers cut ties with before the season, or even trade to find a roster upgrade.

Could The Lakers Move The Young Guard Before The Season?

At first, the Lakers trading James might sound unrealistic. He hasn't proved much in the NBA so far, and many think his value still stems from his name rather than anything he's shown on the court through his first two seasons in the league.

That's reasonable, but according to Heavy's Sean Deveney, many rival teams don't see James that way.

"Other teams have taken notice of James, too, though," Deveney reported . "The Lakers will need to drop one player from the roster, and the presumption — rightly — is that it's likely to be Dalton Knecht. But don't rule out a Bronny James trade, not because the Lakers are seeking to dump him but because he could bring in draft assets–even a second rounder or two, which is what James would bring."

"There's definitely interest there," one executive reportedly told the insider. "He's gotten much better in a short period. He knows his role, and it's hard to find young guys who just want to excel in their role."

In the time since that report, teams like the Brooklyn Nets , Los Angeles Clippers , Charlotte Hornets , and Phoenix Suns have all emerged as potential trade partners with the Lakers for James.

Still, for now it's just rumors and buzz, nothing confirmed yet.

It remains to be seen how much value Los Angeles feels James has. On the outside, they remain committed to him. But if that were truly the case, he wouldn't be named alongside Knecht and Hardy as one of the top candidates to be off the roster before the season starts.

It's also uncertain if a trade is best for James' career in the NBA. He has a spotlight playing in the Purple and Gold, but he could see a bigger role and more room to grow on a different team.

If the Lakers are serious about trading James, despite what his preseason box score against the Kings shows, that could make him a viable candidate to be moved. But at the same time, if the Lakers feel he played well, that might give them another reason to keep him around.

For the time being, James is on the Lakers and has a guaranteed contract for the 2026-27 season, but that doesn't guarantee his safety on the roster for the next few weeks or months.

articles.title: WNBA Playoffs Deliver Most-Watched First Round Ever
articles.summary: Game 3 between the Aces and Fever drew 2.3 million viewers.
articles.body:
WNBA playoff viewership is off to a record start.

The first round of the WNBA playoffs averaged 1.3 million viewers over 10 games on ESPN, Prime Video, and USA Network, the league announced Tuesday, making it the most-watched opening round in history.

Viewership is up 37% compared to last year, when the first round drew an average of 944,000 people over 11 games on ABC, ESPN, and ESPN2. It's also up 17% compared to 2024's first-round ratings record of 1.1 million average viewers over eight games. That was Caitlin Clark's rookie year and the first time she ever played in the playoffs.

The do-or-die Game 3 between the Las Vegas Aces and Indiana Fever on Thursday was the most-watched game of the first round, drawing 2.3 million viewers. That's the second-most-watched first-round game ever behind Game 2 of the 2024 series between the Fever and Connecticut Sun, which drew 2.5 million viewers.

The 2026 WNBA Playoffs are the league's first since signing a new media rights deal worth more than $3 billion . ESPN previously had exclusive rights to the playoffs, but this new deal splits the postseason among four partners: ESPN, Amazon, NBC, and Versant.

The playoff numbers come after another strong regular season for the WNBA, which also saw continued viewership growth across many of its broadcast partners. ESPN was up 17% compared to last year, while CBS saw a 9% increase.

articles.title: Giannis finally takes Kaseya Center court for Heat, adding buzz to benefit scrimmage, ‘It’s good to be on this side’
articles.summary: MIAMI — Typically, an intrasquad scrimmage during the NBA preseason merits a yawn. This one, however, felt different. Because Tuesday night’s Red, White & Pi...
articles.body:
MIAMI — Typically, an intrasquad scrimmage during the NBA preseason merits a yawn.

This one, however, felt different. Because Tuesday night's Red, White & Pink Game marked the first time Giannis Antetokounmpo was in action in Heat colors on the Heat's court.

Yes, there were bigger messages to be shared, with the game benefiting Baptist Health Herbert Wertheim Cancer Institute, as a tribute to those fighting and those who have beaten breast cancer.

So, good cause, good vibes and a low-stress means to introduce Antetokounmpo to the home crowd.

The event began with Heat players introduced while accompanied by survivors, patients and doctors, entering the court with the guests of honor, with Antetokounmpo introduced immediately before Bam Adebayo.

Antetokounmpo addressed the crowd before the game.

"I feel good. This is my first time being out here with fans," he said. "It's good to be on this side. I feel good. I'm excited. I'm motivated. I'm working hard. I'm locked in."

Of the event, Adebayo related it the approach of coach Erik Spoelstra, "Spo always has this thing about sharing in success. This night is about that."

Which Spoelstra then stressed when he spoke on the court.

"This night is about the survivors and everybody who is dealing with this," he said.

Six Degrees of Heat from Tuesday night's scrimmage:

1. The event: Antetokounmpo and Adebayo opened alongside each other, in a first five rounded out by Davion Mitchell, Klay Thompson and Simone Fontecchio.

Four of those five started Saturday's preseason-opening victory over the Toronto Raptors, with Fontecchio filling in for Saturday starter Andrew Wiggins, who missed the scrimmage due to illness.

During the opening period Mitchell actually dunked (albeit in the lack of defense). He last dunked in an NBA game during the 2022-23 season while with the Sacramento Kings. Mitchell then dunked again in the second half.

That was followed by a volley of 3-pointers from Adebayo, who played in a pink do-rag.

After the opening period, Antetokounmpo, known for his fascination for dad jokes, found himself in a joke-off with Adebayo.

He was asked by Adebayo, "What did the fast tomato say to the slow tomato?" With Antetokounmpo unable to answer, Adebayo said, "Ketchup."

Other humor on the night included Nikola Jovic and second-round pick Ryan Conwell attempting to score on Antetokounmpo.

2. Meaningful moments: Although teammates also were the opponent Tuesday, a pair of Heat newcomers said the scrimmage still held meaning.

"An opportunity to bring our families, our kids, to be able to see what we do," Antetokounmpo said. "You just see that a little bit behind the scenes of, like, when Daddy says, 'I'm going to work,' what that actually means."

Said Thompson, "It's really cool that the fan who might not be able to come to the amount of games they like gets a chance to come see us up close and personal. So it means a great deal for us, and obviously for a great cause."

3. Sitting out: Due to illness, neither Pelle Larsson nor Wiggins were available for the scrimmage, with injured Dru Smith and Keshad Johnson also missing the event.

Despite being sidelined by a strained right hamstring sustained last week in camp, an injury that is expected to have him out for weeks, Johnson did light shooting before the scrimmage.

Johnson is one of three Heat players under two-way contract, the NBA maximum, with teams allowed to swap out two-way contracts at any time without a hit against the salary cap.

Smith sustained a strained right calf during camp and also is expected to be out multiple weeks.

He walked onto the court during the pregame introductions without any type of limited gait.

4. As expected: Antetokounmpo did his pre-scrimmage drill work with assistant coach Vin Baker, who accompanied Antetokounmpo from the Bucks this summer.

Malik Allen, the Heat's long-time big-man coach, handled the pregame drilling with centers Adebayo and Nick Richards.

5. New voice: Tuesday marked the first time on the microphone for Gale Nelson as the team's new public-address announcer.

Nelson replaced long-time Heat voice Michael Baiamonte, who retired following last season.

Nelson was briefly introduced to the crowd prior to the start of the scrimmage, offering a booming presence similar to Baiamonte's sometimes-over-the-top approach.

Following the introductions, Nelson said of the night's guests of honor, "Thank you for being an inspiration to us all."

6. Up next: Up next for the Heat is a run of three consecutive home exhibitions, starting with Thursday night's 7:30 p.m. matchup against the New Orleans Pelicans, with a Saturday 8 p.m. exhibition against the visiting Minnesota Timberwolves to follow.

The Heat then conclude their five-game preseason schedule with an Oct. 14 home game against the Brooklyn Nets and an Oct. 16 road game against the Orlando Magic.

That all leads to opening night of the regular season on Oct. 21 against the visiting Timberwolves.

articles.title: Kristaps Porzingis Health Update Given By Steve Kerr as Warriors Star Out Indefinitely
articles.summary: Kristaps Porzingis is out indefinitely with an undisclosed health issue ahead of the 2026-27 campaign, and Golden State Warriors head coach Steve Kerr offered some insight into how serious the issue is.
articles.body:
Kristaps Porzingis is out indefinitely with an undisclosed health issue ahead of the 2026-27 campaign, and Golden State Warriors head coach Steve Kerr offered some insight into how serious the issue is.

Kerr told reporters Tuesday that he hasn't "seen him yet" and added that it's "definitely concerning."

While Porzingis is out indefinitely to start training camp, general manager Mike Dunleavy Jr. told reporters last week that there is still a chance he'll start the season with the team.

"I'm not marking him down as being out to start the season or anything like that. He's just not available this week," he said.

Golden State opened training camp in Hawai'i before playing its first preseason game on Sunday against the Los Angeles Clippers in Honolulu. Porzingis did not travel with the team.

Porzingis has missed a combined 90 games over the past two seasons because of health issues. In February 2025, when he was with the Boston Celtics, he began experiencing a prolonged upper respiratory viral illness.

Ahead of the 2025-26 campaign, Porzingis revealed that he had been diagnosed with POTS, a disease that affects the autonomic nervous system and impacts the nerves that regulate blood flow, according to the Mayo Clinic . It causes symptoms like an overly rapid heartbeat and shortness of breath.

"It hit me, and it hit me like a truck," he told Fred Katz of The Athletic last October. "The breathing wasn't good. I did everything I could potentially to feel as good as I could, but my engine wasn't running the way I wanted."

Before his latest setback, Porzingis had been in the Warriors' facility taking part in offseason events.

"He's been participating in everything," Dunleavy said. "It just kind of popped up."

Porzingis, who joined the Warriors last year after being traded by the Atlanta Hawks, is an effective big man when available. He put up 16.7 points, 5.2 rebounds and 1.2 blocks per game across 32 contests last year.

Unfortunately for Porzingis, staying on the court consistently has been a struggle for him over the past few seasons.

articles.title: Bronny James, Yaxel Lendeborg's Final Box Score Stats, Highlights from Lakers vs. Warriors Preseason
articles.summary: The Golden State Warriors wrapped up a 124-98 blowout win over the Los Angeles Lakers in the preseason on Tuesday night.
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors wrapped up a 124-98 blowout win over the Los Angeles Lakers in the preseason on Tuesday night.

Bronny James started for the Lakers in the contest, while Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg remained part of Golden State's starting five.

With the Lakers missing several players including Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves, James was on the floor for 21 minutes against Golden State.

Despite missing both of his three-point attempts, he shot 2-of-3 from inside the arc. James also committed three turnovers compared to his team-high five assists.

Lendeborg scored just four points on 1-of-6 shooting in his preseason debut, but fared much better on Tuesday.

The No. 11 overall pick in the 2026 NBA draft shot 7-of-11 from the field and 2-of-3 from three-point territory, showcasing his athletic finishing around the rim as well as his ability to space the floor.

While it's important not to put too much stock into the plus-minus of a single preseason game, it's still worth noting that the Warriors outscored the Lakers by 21 points in Lendeborg's 21 minutes of action.

Golden State and Los Angeles will face off again to begin the regular season on Oct. 21.

articles.title: Curry le demuestra a los Lakers que son mucho menos sin Doncic: "No se trata solo de mí"
articles.standfirst: Los Golden State Warriors ganan con solvencia a Los Angeles Lakers, que jugaron sin Luka Doncic, en al pretemporada NBA
articles.summary: Los Golden State Warriors ganan con solvencia a Los Angeles Lakers, que jugaron sin Luka Doncic, en al pretemporada NBA
articles.body: Los Angeles Lakers jugaron sin Luka Doncic 24 horas de ganar a los Sacramento Kings con el esloveno, y lo pagaron. Los Golden State Warriors pasaron por encima de los angelinos para imponerse 124-98 en el Chase Center de San Francisco en la pretemporada NBA. Stephen Curry (16 puntos con 3 de 6 en triples en 14 minutos), Yaxel Lendeborg (17 puntos y 9 rebotes) y Brandin Podziemski (16 puntos) lideraron el triunfo de los de la Bahía de San Francisco. Los mejores de los Lakers fueron Sandro Mamukelashvili (15 puntos), Jaden Hardy (13 puntos), Quentin Grimes (12 puntos) y Dalton Knecht (11 puntos). Adou Thiero sumó 7 puntos y 4 rebotes en la derrota de sus Lakers. El poderoso alero de 22 años y 2,01 m., que tiene un salto vertical de 117 centímetros, protagonizó un espectacular mate que asustó al público por la estremecedora posición en la que se quedó su pierna derecha al aterrizar. "Fue una caída aparatosa, pero estoy bien. Sin duda prestaré más atención a eso, aunque hay situaciones en las que resulta difícil preocuparse por el aterrizaje. Pero, desde luego, es algo que sigo teniendo presente", declaró tras el partido para tranquilizar a la afición. Sobre su capacidad de salto Thiero compartió que "he ido mejorando en ese aspecto a lo largo del verano y aprendiendo a identificar cuándo utilizar mi capacidad atlética... También hay momentos en los que puedo saltar rodeado de tres jugadores y aun así lograr un mate. Se trata, simplemente, de tener confianza en mí mismo y saber qué puedo hacer en cada situación". Los Lakers jugaron sin Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves, Walker Kessler y Collin Sexton. Doncic, que recibió un golpe en el muslo y no jugó contra los Warriors por decisión técnica, reconoció tras ganar a los Kings que "Me sentí muy bien. El baloncesto es una de las mejores cosas de mi vida y lo echaba mucho de menos. Creo que han pasado cinco o seis meses. Volver a jugar y competir es muy divertido para mí, y estoy realmente feliz de haber regresado". "No se trata solo de mí, sino de cómo se siente el equipo al jugar unido. Hemos demostrado que podemos jugar muy bien, especialmente en la transición de defensa a ataque, pero siento que todavía tenemos mucho margen de mejora. Estoy muy contento de formar parte de este equipo", apuntó.

articles.body: LeBron James ha respondido a los rumores de que había abroncado a Joel Embiid, su compañero en los Philadelphia 76ers, por llegar tarde a un entrenamiento de los 76ers. LeBron James y Joel Embiid afrontan su primera temporada en unos Sixers que aspiran a todo con Jaylen Brown, Tyrese Maxey y VJ Edgecombe. articles.summary: Khalifa Diop busca un hueco en la NBA con Cleveland Cavaliers
articles.body: Los Cleveland Cavaliers han pasado por España para ponerse a punto de cara a la nueva temporada. La franquicia NBA ha trabajado en las impresionantes instalaciones 'The Sanctuary' en la Costa del Sol. Khalifa Diop, uno de los nuevos fichajes del conjunto de Ohio, ha pasado por los micrófonos de 'Nos Gusta el Basket'. "El nivel de comunicación es increíble, tienen personas en todos los sitios y eso ayuda mucho al jugador", apuntó el senegalés con pasado en Gran Canaria o Baskonia, del que sigue muy pendiente. "El otro día estuve hablando con Paolo Galbiatti, es un tío que me ha ayudado mucho el año pasado también fuera de la cancha. Estoy también en contacto con mis compañeros y siguiéndolos". El pívot, que se encuentra en la parte final de su puerta a punto compartirá vestuario con jugadores de la talla de James Harden o Donovan Mitchell "Ellos tienen mucha experiencia e intentan ayudarte en cada jugada o en el vídeo y voy a aprender mucho de ellos", comentó Khalifa, que cumple un sueño con su fichaje por los CAVS. "Siempre ha sido mi objetivo, cada verano me iba con ellos a entrenar, a hacer técnica individual y este verano intenté todo lo posible para estar con ellos y al final lo he conseguido. Como si tengo que dormir en el pabellón, haré todo lo que esté en mi mano para estar muchos años en la NBA", confesó. Por delante le queda una dura pretemporada para convencer al 'madrileño' Atkinson de que tiene hueco en el equipo. "El entrenador me ha pedido que ayude en todo lo que pueda, sobre todo en rebote y en la defensa del bloqueo directo. Este es un gran equipo y yo estoy aquí para ayudarles a conseguir los objetivos", explicó. En Cleveland, el pívot también comparte equipo con un jugador al que conoce a la perfección de muchos duelos en Liga Endesa, un Mario Hezonja que también pelea por un hueco entre los elegidos. "¿Qué te voy a decir de Mario? Es uno de los mejores jugadores en Europa, MVP de la Liga Endesa y está más que preparado para la NBA", expresó.

articles.title: El Panathinaikos atiza al Olympiacos por las negociaciones con la NBA
articles.standfirst: Lo hace a través de su propietario Dimitris Giannakopoulos en redes sociales
articles.summary: Lo hace a través de su propietario Dimitris Giannakopoulos en redes sociales
articles.body: Los ecos de la Asamblea de los propietarios de la Euroliga en el Lago Como no se han disipado. Allí se analizaron algunos temas de enorme calado para el futuro del baloncesto europeo, como por ejemplo la conversión de las 13 licencias propietarias de la competición en franquicias o la inminente expansión de la Euroliga. Y también la propuesta de la NBA para ir de la mano en una futura competición. Esa propuesta quedó desestimada por los 13 equipos, aunque la negativa no fue igual en unos y en otros. Hubo un sector más duro como el Barça que tildó la propuesta de "broma" o como el Olympiacos, que intentó impulsar una votación para cortar por completo la comunicación con la NBA y olvidarse de negociar. Esos equipos, principalmente el vigente campeón, han sido objetivo del mensaje en redes de Dimitris Giannakopoulos, propietario del Panathinaikos, que aprovecha la ocasión para atizar a su rival. El PAO griego forma parte del grupo de equipos que, sin estar conforme con la propuesta, están dispuestos a seguir negociando. Hay más, entre ellos, el Real Madrid, el Fenerbahce y el Bayern Múnich. El Madrid de hecho habló de dar 30 días a la NBA para que mejorara su oferta, aunque algunos equipos desestimaron también esa opción. Horas después de que la Asamblea acabara, Ginnakopoulos publicó su mensaje en las redes. En él se refiere a los equipos más beligerantes con la propuesta de la NBA, pero sólo mencionó al Olympiacos y les puso como ejemplo de equipos que no querían expandir el baloncesto europeo. La frase final de "el baloncesto no es un juguete para niños ricos" es lapidaria. Este es el mensaje completo de Giannakouloulos: "JUGADORES Y ENTRENADORES AFICIONADOS PROPIETARIOS DIRECTIVOS DEL BALONCESTO EUROPEO Todos juntos hemos convertido el deporte que amamos en una competición en la que la NBA —repito, la NBA, la mejor liga del mundo— quiere invertir y hacer que la Euroliga forme parte de su mundo. Con enorme respeto, pero también orgullosos de lo que finalmente hemos conseguido (sin Jordi), debemos encontrar juntos una solución. Posiciones como la de Olympiacos actualmente, y la de un par de equipos más, no tienen ningún interés en expandir el deporte del baloncesto. Siguen creyendo que el éxito consiste en cuánto dinero pierdes al final del año. El baloncesto no es un juguete de niños ricos".

articles.title: Aday Mara cae de pie en los Thunder: "Hay que estar en muy buena forma para hacer esas cosas"
articles.standfirst: El pívot español debuta en pretemporada, es alabado por su técnico y levanta a sus compañeros del banquillo con sus acciones
articles.summary: El pívot español debuta en pretemporada, es alabado por su técnico y levanta a sus compañeros del banquillo con sus acciones
articles.body: El primer partido de pretemporada de Aday Mara con los Thunder no pudo dejar mejor impresión en sus compañeros, en su entrenador Mark Daigneault, en la prensa de Oklahoma y en los aficionados. Saliendo de titular y en sólo 18 minutos en pista, el pívot español hizo 12 puntos sin fallo (5/5 en tiros de campo), 12 puntos, nueve rebotes, tres asistencias y tres tapones. En ese tiempo mostró la amplitud de su repertorio. Los de Oklahoma, sin muchos de sus referentes, acabaron perdiendo por 110-116. El técnico de los Thunder destacó sobre todo el esfuerzo que ha hecho Mara durante el verano para ponerse a tono. "Trabajó muy duro desde el final de la Summer League hasta que volvió a Oklahoma y luego hasta el training camp. Son muchos días los que acumuló con la cabeza gacha, trabajando en su acondicionamiento físico y se notó esta noche", contó Daigneault sobre su discípulo, elegido en el puesto 12 del último draft. Tanto en ataque como en defensa, Mara pudo mostrar sus principales recursos: una gran visión de juego y capacidad de pase, canastas sencillas haciendo valer su altura y sus fundamentos técnicos e intimidación. "Obviamente es un jugador muy efectivo por su nivel de habilidad en ataque y luego por su impacto en defensa, pero hay que estar en muy buena forma para hacer esas cosas y él está trabajando para eso", dijo el el entrenador de los Thunder, que resumió en una frase: "Fue un inicio muy bueno para él". Al inicio del segundo cuarto, el pívot maño dejó una acción de las que caracterizan su juego. Puso un tapón bajo su aro, salió a la contra, recibió un pase en carrera y enfiló el aro para dejar una preciosa bandeja en extensión. Con 2,21 metros de altura, no hay muchos jugadores en la NBA capaces de hacerlo. Chet Holmgren, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Jalen Williams y el resto del banquillo se levantaron para celebrarlo. Algunos con gesto de incredulidad y otros imitando la brillante finalización de Mara. "Lo vi, lo vi. Fue gracioso. Estaban haciendo el gesto de 'finger roll'. Yo sólo estaba allí, pillé el balón, vi el aro y creía que ni podía hacer un mate, así que intenté hacer una bandeja. Fue divertido", aseguró el jugador español. Fue su primer partido de pretemporada y no conviene sobrerreaccionar, pues la temporada regular es otra cosa, pero empezar mostrando a todos de lo que eres capaz es una noticia extraordinaria.

articles.title: El final de una era: el AS Mónaco desaparece 17 meses después de jugar la final de la Euroliga
articles.standfirst: El club monegasco anuncia que no puede hacer frente a sus obligaciones de pago y que suspenderá sus operaciones
articles.summary: El club monegasco anuncia que no puede hacer frente a sus obligaciones de pago y que suspenderá sus operaciones
articles.body: El 25 de mayo del año pasado, el AS Mónaco se quedó a las puertas de ser campeón de la Euroliga por primera vez. El Fenerbahce le impidió coronarse como campeón continental. Han pasado 17 meses desde que aquello y ahora la entidad acaba de anunciar que no puede hacer frente a sus obligaciones de pago y que suspenderá sus operaciones. A un crecimiento extraordinario que le hizo rozar la gloria le ha sucedido una vertiginosa caída. "A pesar de todos los esfuerzos realizados, el AS Monaco Basket se encuentra en estado de suspensión de pagos", ha publicado el club en un comunicado dirigido a sus seguidores. A estas alturas, después de haber buscado fórmulas para sobrevivir y haber luchado en muchas estancias deportivas, sólo queda la esperanza de la refundación. El AS Mónaco arrastraba 24 millones de euros de deuda acumulada durante la gestión del magnate Alexey Fedorychev, cuyas cuentas quedaron congeladas con la guerra de Ucrania. Comenzaron los impagos, amenazas de huelga, la marcha de jugadores e incluso del entrenador Vassilis Spanoulis, que abandonó a mitad de la convulsa temporada pasada. Y pese a las muy complejas circunstancias, el equipo luchó en la pista, en ocasiones afrontando algunos encuentros con sólo con siete jugadores profesionales, para ganar las cuatro competiciones que estaban en juego en el baloncesto francés. La ayuda del Principado, permitió que el club acabará la campaña. Después comenzó la desbandada de jugadores y ninguna de las propuestas económicas recibidas, incluida la del exNBA Jamal Mashburn, llegó a fructificar. Las instituciones del deporte francés no consideraron viable ninguno de esos planes. Primero se le cerró la puerta de la élite del baloncesto galo. Después de la Eurocup, donde ha sido sustituido por el Bosna Sarajevo. Ahora, las últimas. El comunicado en el que el club se declara en bancarrota afirma que el futuro del baloncesto masculino en Mónaco ahora recae en la asociación ASM, su directiva, entrenadores, jugadores juveniles y el primer equipo, que compite en la Nationale 3. Así acaba la historia de una entidad que en los últimos 12 años ganó la Eurocopa en 2021, lo que permitió su acceso a la Euroliga en la siguiente edición. También conquistó tres Ligas de Francia, cuatro Copas de Líderes, dos Copas de Francia y una Supercopa. En 2025 acarició el cielo de ser campeón de la Euroliga, pero ahora ha terminado en los infiernos.

articles.title: El Maccabi jugará en Chipre sus partidos como local en la Euroliga y el Real Madrid será el primero en ir
articles.standfirst: El club macabeo se muda de Belgrado a Limasol, aunque su pretensión es volver a jugar los partidos en Tel Aviv
articles.summary: El club macabeo se muda de Belgrado a Limasol, aunque su pretensión es volver a jugar los partidos en Tel Aviv
articles.body: El Maccabi Tel Aviv está un poquito más cerca de cumplir su pretensión de volver a disputar sus partidos de Euroliga en Israel. Al menos en términos geográficos, el conjunto hebreo se acercado a su casa, pues en lugar de jugar en Belgrado como hasta ahora lo hará en Chipre. Desde los atentados de Hamás el 7 de octubre de 2023 y la posterior respuesta israelí, el Maccabi había establecido en Serbia su sede europea. Yiannis Ioannou, presidente de la Organización Deportiva de Chipre, anunció la decisión del Maccabi de jugar sus partidos como local en la Euroliga en el Spyros Kyprianou de Limasol, un pabellón de infausto recuerdo para la selección española, pues ahí disputó la primera fase del Eurobasket 2025 tras la cual fue eliminada. La instalación tiene capacidad para 8.000 espectadores, pero el aforo se verá reducido a sólo 5.000 por medidas de seguridad. Ya fue inspeccionado esta misma semana por las autoridades deportivas de Chipre, la Policía y el propio club israelí. Está previsto que el Maccabi juegue en Chipre su primer partido de Euroliga el próximo 22 de octubre, cuando debe recibir al Real Madrid en la séptima jornada. articles.title: Pedro Martínez: "Yo no soy nadie para pedir paciencia"
articles.standfirst: El entrenador del Real Madrid asume la peliaguda situación de su equipo al iniciar la Euroliga con tres derrotas seguidas
articles.summary: El entrenador del Real Madrid asume la peliaguda situación de su equipo al iniciar la Euroliga con tres derrotas seguidas
articles.body: Tres derrotas, cero margen para mirar hacia otro lado. El Real Madrid afronta ante el Partizan su primer partido de Euroliga en el Movistar Arena con la necesidad de reaccionar ya. Pedro Martínez sabe que el exigente entorno blanco no entiende de esperas y, por eso, lanza un mensaje tan contundente como revelador: “Yo no soy nadie para pedir paciencia”, dio en rueda de prensa. El técnico no quiere excusas ni vendas ante un arranque que ha colocado al Madrid en una situación incómoda. “Lo que pido es trabajar en el día a día, hacer las cosas con esfuerzo y estar centrados en hacer lo que depende de nosotros lo mejor posible”, explicó. La palabra paciencia no entra en su discurso. Sí el trabajo, la autocrítica y la obligación de mejorar. Martínez, sin embargo, no percibe un vestuario presa del nerviosismo. “No los veo especialmente nerviosos, los veo preocupados y responsabilizados”, aseguró. Le gusta la mentalidad de sus jugadores y destaca que están intentando defender mejor. Pero también admite que las tres derrotas europeas generan “un poco más de intranquilidad”. Y en el Madrid, esa intranquilidad puede crecer rápido. El entrenador pide separar el resultado del análisis, aunque sabe perfectamente dónde está. “Los resultados no pueden condicionarlo todo”, sostiene. Pero tampoco quiere esconderse detrás de un discurso optimista: “No podemos ponernos una venda delante de los ojos”. El Madrid necesita recuperar sensaciones, continuidad y regularidad antes de que el mal comienzo empiece a pesar demasiado en la grada. El Partizan, dirigido por el español Joan Peñarroya, Aparece como una prueba de máxima exigencia y también como una oportunidad. Un rival “muy físico” y “tremendamente agresivo” que llega en un gran momento y obligará al Madrid a elevar su nivel. La respuesta, además, tendrá un escenario especial: el debut europeo en casa, con una afición que puede ser el mejor aliado... pero también un termómetro de la situación. Pedro Martínez ya ha empezado a tocar piezas. Reconoce que, a medida que conoce mejor a sus jugadores, detecta cosas que no les encajan y busca variantes para sacar el máximo rendimiento colectivo. Eso sí, descarta un volantazo: no habrá “un cambio radical” en el planteamiento. Ajustes, sí. Reacción, también. Porque el Madrid necesita encontrar cuanto antes una identidad que todavía está en construcción. Y en ese contexto llega el mensaje definitivo del técnico: “Hay que jugar pensando en el presente”. Ni lamentarse por el 0-3 ni esperar a que la situación se arregle sola. El Madrid necesita una victoria que frene la inquietud antes de que se transforme en nerviosismo. En un club donde ganar es una exigencia, la paciencia nunca puede ser una coartada.

She has now asked a New York court to intervene over the financial support she says remains unpaid.Who is Tanya Young Williams?Tanya Young Williams is an American attorney, businesswoman, television personality and advocate. She became widely known through her marriage to former NBA star Jayson Williams.The couple married in 2000 and have two daughters together, Tryumph Williams and Whizdom Williams. Their family life later faced serious challenges, particularly after Jayson became involved in the highly publicized 2002 shooting case involving his limousine driver, Costas “Gus” Christofi.Jayson was charged in connection with Christofi’s death. He later pleaded guilty to aggravated assault and served time in prison. Tanya remained by his side during the legal proceedings, but their relationship eventually deteriorated.Tanya first filed for divorce in 2009. At the time, she accused Jayson of cruel treatment and made allegations involving domestic abuse, alcohol abuse, threats and infidelity. Jayson’s attorney denied the allegations and accused Tanya of making false claims to pressure him into a settlement. The divorce was never finalized, leaving their legal relationship unresolved for years.Now, as reported by TMZ, Tanya has filed a new court action in New York. She claims Jayson did not provide financial support for their daughters during his imprisonment from 2010 to 2012. According to her account, payments began after a 2015 settlement but stopped after about two years.Tanya says the missed payments have left Jayson “hundreds of thousands of dollars in arrears.”She also claims that Jayson has been largely absent from their daughters’ lives for years. According to Tanya, he refused to communicate with them despite repeated attempts by the daughters to reach out. She says efforts to resolve the issue with his representatives failed, leading her to seek court intervention.Tanya has built a career away from basketball. She is the CEO and co-founder of Pivot Treatment & Wellness Centers, where she works in the addiction recovery and wellness space. She has also been involved in efforts to reduce the stigma surrounding addiction and mental health.She has worked as a legal analyst and commentator for networks including CNN, HLN and KTLA. She has also contributed to publications including HuffPost and The Daily Beast.Tanya became a television personality after appearing on the first season of VH1’s Basketball Wives LA.
