articles.title: Lakers' JJ Redick Clarifies Perceived LeBron James Shade After Saying Pieces Now 'Fit Together'
articles.summary: Los Angeles Lakers coach J.J. Redick expanded on recent comments expressing excitement about his current roster, which seemed like potential shade toward LeBron James, when speaking with The Athletic's Sam Amick.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Lakers coach J.J. Redick expanded on recent comments expressing excitement about his current roster, which seemed like potential shade toward LeBron James, when speaking with The Athletic's Sam Amick .

Redick told reporters Sept. 24, after James left to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers in free agency, he considered the current version of the Lakers "the first time in my three years here that I feel like the pieces actually fit together."

The Lakers coach more recently told Amick that comment regarded new depth options behind Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves.

"When I said the pieces fit, that's more about having depth, having multiple ballhandlers besides Luka and AR, having more shooting, more volume shooting, having an elite rim protector — the combination of all those pieces," Redick said, according to Amick.

Redick continued, per Amick: "And it's having great wing defenders. I really believe in our wing group. I believe in their defense. I believe in their ability to make open 3s."

He added the Lakers can't "become a championship team" in September but "have to become one throughout the season," per Amick.

The Lakers completely overhauled their roster this summer, parting ways with Rui Hachimura, Deandre Ayton, Jaxson Hayes, Marcus Smart and Luke Kennard along with James.

Those moves coincided with the franchise bringing in Walker Kessler, Quentin Grimes, Jaden Hardy, Collin Sexton, Ziaire Williams, Sandro Mamukelashvili, Kevon Looney and Matisse Thybulle.

Sexton and Grimes can function as ballhandlers behind Reaves and Dončić, Amick noted. Kessler will be asked to provide rim protection while Williams and Thybulle will be tasked with defending from the wings.

The Lakers showed off the shooting volume Redick mentioned in an Oct. 5 preseason opener against the Sacramento Kings, during which a roster resting some starters but playing Dončić for 16 minutes shot 45 percent from deep on 44 attempts.

Redick will now be tasked with finalizing which players will be starting alongside Reaves, Dončić and Kessler ahead of his team's Oct. 21 regular-season opener against Stephen Curry and the visiting Golden State Warriors.

articles.title: NBA Scout Drops Brutally Honest Take on JJ Redick's Comments About Lakers' Improved Defense
articles.summary: JJ Redick's assessment that the Los Angeles Lakers have the talent, particularly on defense, to become a championship-level team during the 2026-27 season is not shared by at least one person who works in the NBA.
articles.body:
JJ Redick's assessment that the Los Angeles Lakers have the talent, particularly on defense, to become a championship-level team during the 2026-27 season is not shared by at least one person who works in the NBA.

An anonymous scout for a rival team had a one-word response for The Athletic's Sam Amick when asked if they felt the Lakers had the pieces in place to win a title this season.

LeBron rejects rumor he yelled at new teammate

Redick told reporters at the start of training camp he has confidence in this new-look roster gelling over the course of the season to become a title contender.

"I really believe in our wing group," Redick said (h/t Amick). "I believe in their defense. I believe in their ability to make open 3s. (But) you don't become a championship team (in late September). You have to become one throughout the season."

This offseason saw the Lakers go all-in on building the team around Luka Dončić in ways they couldn't before because LeBron James was still a huge presence.

The Lakers' invested heavily to bring in Walker Kessler, Quentin Grimes and Sandro Mamukelashvili. They also gave Austin Reaves a four-year, $185 million contract to keep him in free agency.

Kessler stands out as the key to determining how high the Lakers' ceiling is this season. He is the first rim-running center Dončić has played with since being acquired by Los Angeles.

The 25-year-old Kessler has been an elite rim protector over the past two seasons, though that comes with some caveats because he has only played 63 games during that period.

Kessler's health will be paramount because Dončić and Austin Reaves in the backcourt are not known for their defensive capabilities.

Grimes has a strong defensive reputation , though he struggled on that end of the floor during his time with the Philadelphia 76ers. Matisse Thybulle can provide wing defense off the bench.

The Lakers haven't finished in the top 10 in defensive rating since the 2020-21 season when they ranked No. 1. They haven't ranked higher than 15th in each of the last two seasons.

There hasn't been an NBA champion that ranked outside the top 10 in defensive rating since the 2022-23 Denver Nuggets. They overcame their limitations on that end of the court by having the fourth-best offense for a championship team in league history.

The 2025-26 New York Knicks had the second-worst defensive rating for an NBA champion, behind only that Nuggets team, but they were seventh in the league in that category.

articles.title: Lakers' JJ Redick Not Concerned With 'Perception' After Bold Comments, 'I Don't Sugarcoat It'
articles.summary: Los Angeles Lakers coach JJ Redick elaborated on his optimistic attitude toward the team heading into the 2026-27 NBA season.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Lakers coach JJ Redick elaborated on his optimistic attitude toward the team heading into the 2026-27 NBA season.

During a press conference last month, Redick asserted the Lakers will "develop as a team into a championship-level team this year." He told The Athletic's Sam Amick he wants to set a tone internally and is less concerned with how those outside of the organization react.

"You've got to get things out in the open," the coach said. "We look at this every day. I don't sugarcoat it.

LeBron rejects rumor he yelled at new teammate

"Those teams (like New York, San Antonio and Oklahoma City) deserve to be perceived that way, (but) I don't care. It doesn't matter — the perception of us. We're on our own path. We are on our journey. That's exciting to me."

Few would consider the Lakers to be championship favorites.

Los Angeles didn't have a path to properly replace LeBron James, and it's betting a lot on an oft-injured center (Walker Kessler) to cover up defensive deficiencies on the perimeter.

The Lakers sit 12th in Bleacher Report's NBA power rankings prior to the preseason.

Kessler, for his part, said he agrees with Redick's overall assessment "no question."

"Undoubtedly," he said, per Amick. "I think we have a lot of great tools and a lot of versatility, and I think that the guys are getting along, and I think connection makes championship teams. We definitely can be a contender."

Realistically, failing to win a championship shouldn't be deemed a disappointment for the Lakers if they have a strong regular season and advance a few rounds in the playoffs.

But the consequence of having a star as big as Luka Dončić is that the expectations climb to an often unrealistic level. The clock is ticking, too, when Dončić is eligible for free agency in 2028.

Should L.A. not look like a "championship-level team" on the court three years into Redick's tenure, the franchise might face some difficult questions next summer.

articles.title: Oregon's Dana Altman Retires Less Than 1 Month Before Start of CBB Season
articles.summary: Less than a month before the start of the 2026-27 college basketball season, Oregon is already dealing with a tumultuous situation after longtime head coach Dana Altman announced his retirement on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Less than a month before the start of the 2026-27 college basketball season, Oregon is already dealing with a tumultuous situation after longtime head coach Dana Altman announced his retirement on Wednesday.

Assistant coach Tony Stubblefield will take over as interim head coach.

The Field of 68 first reported the news.

"I've loved every minute of coaching here, and stepping away is difficult and truly painful," Altman said in a statement announcing his retirement. "I love coaching, it's what I know best and what I've been fortunate enough to do for almost five decades. I'm going to miss my coaches, my players and our incredible fans more than I can express. But I know this is the right thing to do at this time."

Altman had coached at Oregon since 2010, establishing the longtime football school as a basketball powerhouse. In 16 seasons at the helm, he led the Ducks to 15 straight 20-win campaigns, with the streak coming to an end with a 12-20 finish in 2025-26. With a record of 382–182, Altman is the winningest head coach in program history.

Oregon earned a berth in the NCAA Tournament nine times under Altman's direction, reaching the Final Four for the second time in program history in 2017. The Ducks also won four Pac-12 regular-season titles and four conference tournament championships during Altman's tenure.

Before his run at Oregon, Altman served as head coach at Marshall (1989-90), Kansas State (1990-94) and Creighton (1994-2010). He had a career record of 792–425 and earned a total of seven Coach of the Year awards across four different conferences.

Stubblefield had originally joined Oregon's coaching staff in Altman's first year in 2010, and he remained a fixture on the bench until 2021. He accepted a head coaching position at DePaul, compiling a 28–54 record over three seasons before returning to Altman's staff with the Ducks in 2024.

Without Altman leading the way, Oregon could need some time to find its footing during the 2026-27 season before eyeing a potential return to the NCAA Tournament.

articles.title: The Athletic column urging Indiana Fever to part ways with Sophie Cunningham draws widespread criticism
articles.summary: Martina Navratilova and thousands online fired back at Candace Buckner's column arguing the Indiana Fever should part ways with Sophie Cunningham.
articles.body: The phrase "80-20 issue" is thrown out quite a bit in spaces such as these. But Tuesday, a 95-5 issue seems to have emerged. The 95% in this case? The people on the internet bashing a piece from The Athletic that attacked WNBA guard Sophie Cunningham. Columnist Candace Buckner argued that the soon-to-be free agent was a "combustible" figure whose "turbulent" opinions were a distraction to the Indiana Fever. Never mind that Cunningham's most publicized stance — that biological males shouldn't compete in female sports — is shared by the vast majority of the country. SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SENDS MESSAGE TO HER HATERS AFTER SAYING MEN DON'T BELONG IN WOMEN'S SPORTS Buckner's conclusion? That the Fever must part ways with Sophie so that they "can go back to being a basketball team." This sparked the public to break out their drivers. Among the most prominent critics teeing off was nine-time Wimbledon winner Martina Navratilova, a staunch advocate of keeping men out of women's spaces. Said the tennis legend on X: "Buckner seems to forget the W in @WNBA stand for women. There was nothing wrong with what Sophie said originally. It’s the response from WNBA that made it blow up. The policy is the problem, not Sophie Cunningham." This is hard to deny. The "circus" Buckner says surrounds Cunningham wouldn't exist if the WNBA could simply define what a woman is. Doing so would have kept former NBA players such as Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White from declaring their intent to enter the WNBA Draft. But the W doesn't want to have that discussion. Its leaders are too afraid of the internal blowback. They opt for the more widespread external blowback instead. Another Buckner critic was podcast host Stephen L. Miller, who focused less on the trans issue and more on the media's hypocrisy. Mocking the Athletic's post on X, Miller wrote: "If the San Francisco 49ers want to go back to being a football team, Colin Kaepernick has to go." KAEPERNICK TELLS 'THE VIEW' THAT NFL OWNERS KEPT HIM OUT OVER POLITICS AND POWER, CLAIMS THEY DONATE TO TRUMP Yes. I can make a Namath-esque guarantee that nobody in media decrying Cunningham as a distraction had that same energy for Kaepernick 10 years ago. Forget that Kaepernick made a conscious decision to enter the political fray whereas Sophie simply answered a question about trans athletes in an ESPN interview. The problem for media pundits isn't that Cunningham has "big opinions," as Buckner said — it's that she has the wrong opinions. But the disdain players and critics have for Sophie is often projected onto her fans as well. There seems to be this idea that Fever supporters are these backward hillbillies filled with hate because they back players embraced in conservative circles. So, you'll get players such as Angel Reese claiming that they heard racist comments from attendees in Indiana, or Brittney Griner saying that the league's "new fans" shouted racial slurs at her. Except, there hasn't been an ounce of evidence that any of this "hate" it taking place in real time. Which led to this rather on-the-nose post from the X account Veritas Explorer, which wrote "The real story was the anti-Fever, racist media campaign led by Jussie Smollett." SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SEES SUPPORT SURGE AFTER STAR PUTS CAREER ON LINE FOR GIRLS SPORTS All in all there were 1.3K comments on The Athletic's tweet linking to Buckner's column against 1.1K likes. That's a standard "ratio" — as the repulsed replies flooded in. What was interesting is that Buckner didn't tweet the column out on her personal account, which she often does. She likely knew what kind of reaction awaited her. To be fair, though, this is X — whose political tenor has shifted rightward since Elon Musk bought the platform four years ago. So maybe the readers over at The Athletic/New York Times were digging the take? Eh...not so much. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! The most "liked" comment (by far) under her column read as follows. "Hold up. I clicked on this article because I wanted to see the basketball reasons why they should trade Cunningham. Turns out there are none, and the issue is because of off the court issues with something she said. And that is just stupid. I currently live in a city with a football team that employs Deshaun Watson, someone who is far far more destructive to the dignity of women and yet he plays and we don’t get constant columns how he should be. The WNBA should be about the top level of Women’s Basketball. Not the top level of women’s basketball who happen to agree with you. That alone will harm this league more than anything." The second-most "liked" comment was more succinct. "Candace had this one in the drafts for 6 months lol. Sophie did nothing wrong." OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD No, she did not. She stood up for what she believed in. And in the wake of this Buckner column, the public stood behind her.

articles.title: EuroLeague teams reject NBA offer to merge into a single Europe operation
articles.summary: PARIS (AP) — EuroLeague basketball owners have rejected a formal offer from the NBA to merge into a single European operation following a meeting in Italy, B...
articles.body:
PARIS (AP) — EuroLeague basketball owners have rejected a formal offer from the NBA to merge into a single European operation following a meeting in Italy, Barcelona confirmed Wednesday.

The decision not to accept the NBA's proposal of a single Europe entity was made Tuesday in Cernobbio during a gathering of the EuroLeague's 13 shareholder clubs. They include Barcelona, Bayern Munich, Real Madrid, Olympiakos, Milan, Tony Parker -owned ASVEL in France and two Istanbul-based clubs.

A statement on the EuroLeague's website said they met to "discuss and align on key strategic decisions regarding the future of their collective property," without mentioning the NBA.

Barcelona told The Associated Press in an emailed response that a formal merger offer from the NBA had been rejected. In a statement, the club confirmed that Barcelona president Joan Laporta attended the meeting and that club owners "took several decisions regarding the future of the competition."

"Among those decisions was the rejection of the NBA's proposal as it currently stands. Should that proposal be amended in the future, the clubs and the EuroLeague will reconsider it," the statement read.

It's not clear how each club voted. The EuroLeague declined to comment and pointed to its initial statement.

The NBA did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The 20-team EuroLeague is comprised of 13 shareholder clubs immune from relegation. The rest either qualify through their domestic leagues or through invitation.

The NBA, in partnership with FIBA, is eying a 16-team model.

French sports daily L'Equipe reported that the NBA offered each future member 400 million euros ($448 million).

At Tuesday's EuroLeague meeting, club owners agreed to move forward with converting the current 10-year licenses into franchises for the shareholder clubs. They also agreed to continue plans to increase the number of franchises.

France's Victor Wembanyama , Greece's Giannis Antetokounmpo and Slovenia's Luka Doncic are among the biggest basketball stars worldwide.

NBA Commissioner Adam Silver reaffirmed in January that the league was pressing forward on plans to bring a new league to Europe.

The NBA was targeting October 2027 as a potential launch date, with franchises paying what is expected to be a substantial entry fee. Media reports indicated the NBA was looking for at least a $500 million fee.

Many European basketball teams, including some in the EuroLeague, have struggled financially. The system has often relied on wealthy owners to cover team debts each year. ___

articles.title: ESPN BPI: Surging Timberwolves Projected 48 Wins, 95.5% Playoff Odds
articles.summary: The NBA preseason is underway, and the Minnesota Timberwolves opener showed plenty of promise. Now, ESPN’s Basketball Power Index is saying encouraging thing...
articles.body:
The NBA preseason is underway, and the Minnesota Timberwolves opener showed plenty of promise. Now, ESPN's Basketball Power Index is saying encouraging things about the team, too. The Wolves finished 49-33 last season, reached the Western Conference semifinals, and are entering 2026-27 with several roster changes. Just how high are the expectations for the Wolves?

ESPN's projection currently lists Minnesota at 47.8 wins and 34.2 losses, and as either the fourth or, more likely, fifth seed in the Western Conference.

That projection places Minnesota eighth, behind the Oklahoma City Thunder, San Antonio Spurs, New York Knicks, Boston Celtics, Detroit Pistons, Denver Nuggets and Cleveland Cavaliers. The Timberwolves are trailing those last teams by only a slim margin, 47.8, compared with 48.7 for Denver and 47.9 for Cleveland.

Oklahoma City leads the table at 60.7 projected wins, while San Antonio is listed at 59.1. New York is third at 51.7, followed by Boston at 51.3. Detroit is projected to win 49.4 games.

Minnesota's 47.8 figure is 1.2 wins below its 49 victories from last season. That says less about an expectation for the Wolves to be worse, and more about other teams getting better.

ESPN Gives Timberwolves 3 Playoff Probabilities

The BPI table lists an overall 95.5% playoff probability for Minnesota. It also lists an 81.1% probability of finishing in the top six and an 18.8% probability of participating in the play-in tournament.

Those figures are displayed separately in ESPN's projection table. Minnesota also has a 1.7% probability of winning its division in the table. The low figure is so low because of sharing their division with the Thunder.

Oklahoma City and San Antonio are both listed with 100% playoff probabilities. Denver is at 96.9%, New York at 97.7%, Boston at 97.2%, and Cleveland at 88.4%.

The Timberwolves averaged 118.0 points last season, seventh in the NBA, and allowed 114.6 points per game. Their 116.8 offensive rating ranked 12th, while their 113.5 defensive rating ranked eighth.

Anthony Edwards put up 28.8 points a night over 61 games. Meanwhile, Rudy Gobert held down the paint with 11.5 rebounds and 1.6 blocks, and Jaden McDaniels chipped in 14.8 points while hitting a really solid 41.2% of his threes.

Minnesota entered the playoffs as the sixth seed, defeated Denver 4-2 in the first round, and then lost 4-2 to San Antonio in the conference semifinals.

The Current Roster Includes LaMelo Ball and Jonathan Kuminga

2026-27 Minnesota roster lists LaMelo Ball , Jonathan Kuminga , Ayo Dosunmu , Trey Lyles , Bones Hyland , Gobert, Edwards, and McDaniels among the team's established players.

Ball averaged 20.1 points and 7.1 assists in 72 games for Charlotte last season while shooting 36.8% from three. Kuminga averaged 12.2 points and 5.6 rebounds in 36 games playing for the Golden State Warriors and Atlanta Hawks.

The roster also includes Joan Beringer , a 19-year-old center, and Isaiah Evans , whom Minnesota drafted in 2026.

The table places Minnesota at 47.8 projected wins, with Denver at 48.7 and Cleveland at 47.9. Philadelphia follows at 47.5, while Houston is listed at 46.7.

Minnesota is listed with an 81.1% probability of finishing in the top six. The table separately lists an 18.8% play-in probability and a 95.5% overall playoff probability.

What comes next is more important for the Timberwolves than another projection. Minnesota opened its preseason against Milwaukee on Oct. 5, giving the Timberwolves their first live-game setting with the reshaped roster.

While that matchup provided early playing-time clues for Ball, Kuminga, and Beringer, Minnesota's Oct. 7 contest against Indiana marks their second exhibition. From there, Minnesota has several more preseason games to test rotations before the regular season begins. Then they'll try to prove that ESPN's projection severely underrates them.

articles.summary: The MLB Playoffs continue today with four teams fighting for their postseason lives. Here's how to watch on TV or streaming.
articles.body:
Today is one of the biggest days of the MLB season. Four teams face elimination in the American League and National League division series on Wednesday. articles.title: Long-time Oregon coach Dana Altman retires less than a month before regular season
articles.summary: Dana Altman led Oregon to a Final Four appearance in 2017.
articles.body:
Less than a month before Oregon's basketball team opens the season, long-time coach Dana Altman is retiring, the school confirmed Wednesday. News of Altman's retirement was initially reported by The Field of 68's Jeff Goodman.

Altman, 68, has worked for the program for 16 seasons, leading the Ducks to nine appearances in the NCAA tournament.

In a statement, Altman confirmed the news and called it "truly painful" to step away from Oregon.

"I have had to make two really tough decisions in my coaching career," said Altman. "The first was leaving Creighton, a place my family and I dearly loved, to come to Oregon. This is the second. I've loved every minute of coaching here, and stepping away is difficult and truly painful. I love coaching, it's what I know best and what I've been fortunate enough to do for almost five decades. I'm going to miss my coaches, my players and our incredible fans more than I can express. But I know this is the right thing to do at this time. I want to thank former AD Pat Kilkenny for giving me a chance here, Phil Knight and Tim Boyle for their constant and unwavering support, my coaches and players past and present, Rob, President Scholz, and of course our amazing fans. It's been the honor of my life to coach the Ducks."

In that same statement, the school announced assistant Tony Stubblefield would serve as the team's interim head coach during the 2026-27 season.

Stubblefield spent over a decade as an assistant under Altman at Oregon before leaving to become DePaul's head coach in 2021. He spent three seasons at DePaul, leading the team to a 28-54 record. Stubblefield was fired in 2024 and returned to Oregon, once again serving as an assistant under Altman.

With the move, Altman caps a fantastic run at Oregon — and overall. In his 16 seasons with the program, Altman won the Pac-12 tournament four times and frequently had his team in the top-25 polls.

His greatest accomplishment with Oregon came during the 2016-17 season, when he led the team to the Final Four. Oregon, a No. 3 seed that year, couldn't topple North Carolina to advance to the final, losing 77-76 . In his 16 seasons at Oregon, Altman posted a 382-182 record and a .677 winning percentage. He won three Pac-12 Coach of the Year awards at the school.

Prior to that, Altman excelled at Creighton, where he won the Missouri Valley Conference tournament six times in 16 seasons. He led Creighton to the NCAA tournament seven times during his tenure and earned two MVC Coach of the Year awards. He went 327-176 over his 16 seasons at Creighton.

Altman also coached at Marshall for one season and Kansas State for four years. He led Kansas State to the NCAA tournament during the 1992-93 season and earned the Big-8 Coach of the Year award for his efforts.

After making the NCAA tournament during the 2024-25 season, Oregon took a massive step back last year. The team went just 12-20 overall. It was the first time Altman finished under .500 at Oregon.
